messages.subject: second parent genotypes missing
messages.body_plain:
hi everybody!
I am a new user of R/qtl and have one basic question. I have the cross
that was done from 2 wild (not an inbred lines) individuals of extreme
phenotypes. F2 was designed by crossing 2 F1 individuals  that were
sequenced for the certain regions and the SNPs that were chosen to
genotype the F2 generation were all heterozygous. I have just
genotypes of one of those parents which is homozygous for all those
loci, so I know the phase of those, but the portion from parent 2
could come  from homozygous or also from  the repulsion phase.
I was wondering if I could use normal F2 inter-cross analysis in R/qtl
in that case and how would I account for something like that?
Thank you in advance!

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] second parent genotypes missing
messages.body_plain:
You need to infer phase.

Likely you'll want to use the cross type "4way", for a phase-known 4-way cross.  There's a bit of discussion about data format in the help file for read.cross(), but for the most part, unfortunately, the R/qtl functionality for analyzing 4-way crosses is not documented.

karl

messages.subject: Multiple QTL Mapping
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

  I have a data base with about 2500 SNPs on the same chromosome and
880 individus whose trait
is known. I would like to use this packages R/qtl to simulate the
necessary number of the QTL.

  First, I only consider the main effect only and all the QTLs are
independent. By using the function stepwiseqtl with an interval about
0.5cM, I simulate the best models with 1 QTL and the correspondent
pLod
is 7.98 but the percentage of the trait explained is very proof (only
3%).  And I obtain 10 models with the number from 1QTL to 10 QTLS.
Every
time, the number of QTl increase, the correspondent pLod is less.
Tthe
model with 10 QTL can explain 16% the variance of the trait but its
pLod
is 2.02.

So I like to know in my case, which model should I chose.

Thank You

Jiqiong QIU

messages.subject: diploid RIL populations
messages.body_plain:
We are planning to use R/QTL for analysis of an diploid RIL population
(RI6) which still contains a fair amount of residual heterozygosity.
Is R/QTL able to deal with residual heterozygosity? My initial
impression is, is that these scores are being ignored.

Thanks,
Richard
